note: Structure templates as data. A beat id is a name the scenario lint already knows (hook, setup, incident, ladder, turn, button, tag), so beats map 1:1 into <!-- beat: ID --> comments. start_s/end_s are for the template's total_s; `episode.py new` scales them to the spec's target. `rules` overrides scenario.Rules fields for the lint run by `episode.py check`.

shorts-45-60-v1.title: Shorts, linear: hook, setup, incident, two ladder rungs, turn, button
shorts-45-60-v1.source: research/shorts_hooks.md section 4, re-cut to the lint's beat names (twist = turn, escalate = ladder)

beats.role: the strongest standalone line or odd image; no context, no greeting
who, where, what is wrong; one fast exchange, one premise
the thing that starts the trouble
escalation 1, mid-video re-hook (new info, new voice or visual change)
escalation 2, worse than 1
the twist: the hook's answer or the hook re-contextualised; not in the last second
the reaction and the last line; a loop bridge back to frame 1

shorts-reverse-open-v1.title: Shorts, reverse open: aftermath first, rewind, the turn pays a different joke
shorts-reverse-open-v1.source: research/shorts_hooks.md section 2 (punchline-in-reverse cold open) and section 4

beats.role: the aftermath: the worst line or image, then a hard cut marks the rewind
forty seconds earlier: who, where, what is wrong
the thing that starts the trouble
escalation 1
escalation 2
the hook line returns with a new meaning; a different joke than the opener
reaction, last line; loop bridge
